item.content: {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=thermodynamic+cost+of+memory+reliability+retention+time&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Sub-Nanometer Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions With Record-High on-Current Density Through Synergistic Microwave Annealing and High-Field Activation.\", \"abstract\": \"High-density memory systems require a high on-state current density (J<sub>on</sub>) to ensure fast read speeds and large sensing margins in cross-point array applications. However, achieving high J<sub>on</sub> in atomically thin ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) remains an unmet challenge, hindered by parasitic interfacial layer (IL), depolarization fields, and phase instability that favors the non-ferroelectric tetragonal phase. Here, a record-high J<sub>on</sub> operation in sub-nanometer FTJs is enabled by combining aggressive device area scaling with low-temperature microwave annealing. This approach effectively suppresses IL growth, reducing the IL thickness from 0.94 to 0.41 nm, and simultaneously enables a robust orthorhombic phase transition under high electric fields (>15 MV cm<sup>-1</sup>) without dielectric breakdown. By leveraging interface engineering and extreme area scaling, ∼0.9 nm FTJ achieves a record-high J<sub>on</sub> exceeding 10<sup>5</sup> A cm<sup>-</sup> <sup>2</sup> at low voltage (∼0.4 V) while maintaining a stable on/off ratio (>15). This strategy also induces exceptional endurance (>10<sup>8</sup> cycles) and retention (projected ∼10 years at 85°C), attributed to the reduced depolarization fields. Furthermore, simulations based on experimental data provide guidelines for achieving ideal FTJ performance at the ultimate scaling limits. Our comprehensive study establishes a clear pathway toward reliable FTJ memory suitable for high-density array applications without additional material complexity.\", \"doi\": \"10.1002/smll.73730\", \"pmid\": \"42107104\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13306945\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1002/smll.73730\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"docume…
